messages.author: d9fe0d8bc73f3799
messages.subject: two matrix and correlation
parts:
Hello,
I'm new to plyr but I find this package wonderful. Now I'm wondering
whether it's possible to calculate correlation between rows of two
matrices, e.g. cor( X[i, ], Y[i, ] ) for every i. Of course I want to
use plyr and avoid loops.

Robert

messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Re: two matrix and correlation
parts:
Here are some ways to do it:

> m1 <- matrix(runif(20),4,5)
> m2 <- m1 + rnorm(20)/10

Map over the row index:

> laply(1:nrow(m1),function(i) cor(m1[i,],m2[i,]))
[1] 0.9890534 0.8604399 0.9242942 0.9884833

Of course, that is no different from core R's sapply in this case:

> sapply(1:nrow(m1),function(i) cor(m1[i,],m2[i,]))
[1] 0.9890534 0.8604399 0.9242942 0.9884833

Map cor over the lists of rows (plyr doesn't have anything corresponding to mapply):

> mapply(cor,alply(m1,1),alply(m2,1))
        1         2         3         4 
0.9890534 0.8604399 0.9242942 0.9884833 

This last approach seems the cleanest in the absence of a multi-array version of aaply (e.g. syntax could be aaply(list(m1,m2),1,cor) or maaply(cor,1,m1,m2) ), but it is much less efficient.

I'd have thought that mlply could solve this, but the best I could do with mlply was the very long and ugly:

as.numeric(mlply(data.frame(a=I(alply(m1,1)),b=I(alply(m2,1))),function(a,b) cor(a[[1]],b[[1]])))

Take advantage of the matrix case of cor:

adply(array(c(m1,m2),c(dim(m1),2)),1,cor)

This looks the most R-like in style to me (and there's probably a better way to build an n+1 -dimension array from two n-dimension ones)....

I'd have expected it to be as fast as the sapply approach, but in fact it is almost as slow as the mapply/alply approach.

               -s
